about: Cold open 0:00 and chapter 3: the check-in scale's display (checkin_hall `scale`). A bar fills past the limit tick, then OVERWEIGHT; no weight is shown. The display sits 2.77-2.92 m away with focus at 2.29 m, f/2.8: 3-4 px of defocus, matched by tex_blur_px; as the push lands on the display, the focus racks onto it (tex_blur_rack), so OVERWEIGHT is crisp when it holds. The push runs from the whole plate (zoom 1.0, centre 1440,810: the only centre a full-plate frame allows) to the display, with the ends written as the frame really shows them (the old start_center 960,540 and end 1761.7,376.6 lay outside the plate's crop at their zooms; the per-frame clamp rode the edge and released at frame 16, a +3.6 to -11.5 px/frame reversal). Now one eased path: the screen moves one way, -6.7 px/frame easing to 0, never reversing. Review 10 (fault 11): it still read as a printed card, with a white keyline inside the bezel. The keyline was the plate's: its lit face runs 3-4 px past the pins (a hairline at about raw 200, then the bezel's dark gap), while the texture darkens its own edges inside them, so the hairline stood out as a line (left edge 172-182 against 115 just inside, top 156-175 against 100). tex_bleed_px 3.5 carries the texture's edge pixels over it, so the face now falls off smoothly into the bezel. glow (sigma 4 plate px, about 3.6 px on screen at the end; gain 0.4) spills the lit face's light onto the bezel, about 6 px wide (left edge 49, 44, 38, 32, 28 down to the bezel's 22), and scale.html screens a faint diagonal reflection of the glass over the face. The bar, its taller over-limit segments, the blink and 'no number' are unchanged.
